extracted.intended_audience: general TV viewers, sitcom fans and Ranker community voters
extracted.subtask_description: A community-voted, ranked listicle of television sitcoms intended to surface the all-time greatest sitcoms based on voter opinion and several visible signals (votes, upvote rate, episode highlights, awards, cultural impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make you smile / immediate comedic payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Vote for the all time greatest sitcoms that never fail to make you smile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary voting instruction: prioritize sitcoms that reliably produce laughter or a smile. This is presented as the core evaluative standard for inclusion/ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popularity / voter consensus (votes & upvote rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: This list is dynamically ranked based on user voting; the order reflects the consensus of our voters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible metrics include total votes (e.g., '54,902 votes') and upvote rate (e.g., '59% upvote rate'), and 'Ranked # by X voters' which serve as scoring signals. The page emphasizes community votes drive the ranking and disclaims paid placements or editorial bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows are valued for introducing memorable characters that stick in cultural memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: Seinfeld's Jerry/George/Elaine/Kramer, Friends' six leads, The Office ensemble. Item descriptions often highlight standout characters as a reason for a show's greatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catchphrases and quotability
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of unforgettable catchphrases and quotable lines contributes to a sitcom's standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly notes shows 'spawned catchphrases that still live on today' (Friends) and references quotable moments from other series as part of cultural impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconic moments / standout episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Iconic scenes or episodes that remain culturally resonant are a metric of quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each show entry links to 'Best Episodes' lists and highlights episode vote counts (e.g., The One Where Everybody Finds Out — 1,645 Votes). Standout episodes are used as evidence supporting a show's rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in comedic storytelling / format
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows that innovate in structure or form (e.g., 'a show about nothing', mockumentary style, narrative devices) are singled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Seinfeld 'redefined comedic storytelling'; The Office 'masterfully employed a mockumentary style'; How I Met Your Mother uses flashbacks and running gags. Innovation is cited as a reason for lasting impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relatability / observational humor
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to turn everyday situations or mundanity into comedic material and to feel relatable to viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office is described as making 'everyday mundanity' into comedic gold; Seinfeld and others are noted for relatable situations. Relatability is portrayed as a key factor in audience attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble strength / performances
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of cast and ensemble interplay (chemistry, standout performers) contributes to a sitcom's appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple entries cite 'all-star cast' or enumerate principal actors (Friends, The Office, Seinfeld, Cheers), implying cast performance and chemistry are important evaluative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and critical recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Emmy Awards, Golden Globes and other accolades are used as signals of a show's legacy and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cheers 'racking up 28 Emmy Awards', The Office 'garnering numerous accolades such as Primetime Emmy Awards and Golden Globe wins.' Awards are presented as evidence supporting high ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity / run length and premiere info
rubrics_metrics.description: A show's length on air and historical placement (premiere date, multi-season runs) are noted as contextual metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include premiere dates and sometimes run lengths (Cheers' 11-year run). Longevity is used as part of the narrative for a show's significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural legacy / enduring influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows that have left an 'indelible mark on television history' or remain 'still quoted today' are prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text emphasizes cultural resonance (memorable characters, catchphrases, iconic moments) and continued relevance as justification for ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisiveness / polarizing reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some shows are identified as divisive among voters (e.g., 'Most divisive: Roseanne').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page surfaces divisiveness as a metric distinct from overall popularity — a show can provoke split opinions even if highly discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative devices and recurring gags
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of running gags, recurring motifs, and particular narrative tricks that define a show's comedic identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How I Met Your Mother is noted for 'running gags' and a framed narrative; episode-level examples (e.g., 'Slapsgiving') illustrate how recurring bits contribute to fan appreciation and ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting / premise and world-building
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinctive setting or premise (workplace, bar, small town) that provides fertile ground for comedy is highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parks and Recreation's Pawnee, Cheers' Boston bar, and The Office's workplace setting are cited as integral to the comedy and the show's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-segment/responsive rankings (filters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rankings may be filtered or viewed by subgroups (region, generation, gender, fanbases) indicating different audiences weigh criteria differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UI options like 'ranked by All voters / rerankers (50) / region / generation / men / women / big bang theory fans' show that demographic resonance and subgroup preferences are explicit dimensions used to evaluate shows.
